Chunk 1 (L3-L9) carries a self-standing claim: shapes-in-session → agent writes a runnable handoff prompt (one skill, with checks) → the deliverable instruction ('What comes back is a prompt, not a plan. Header 'The handoff prompt that grows your kit' (L3) is a literally true summary of the chunk: the chunk instructs producing a prompt to 'run later' that adds 'one skill, with its checks' each time (L5), matching the incremental-growth framing over the prior header's one-shot 'builds your kit'. Nothing in L5-L9 contradicts it.

Checked all six sub-items against L3, L5, L9 (prompt block at L7 exempt as a fenced block, but checked anyway for completeness: 'It scans...', 'It picks...and builds it', 'It makes sure...checks I can run, not reviews I have to do' is an anaphoric three-sentence run introduced by 'It does three things, in order' — each leg names a DISTINCT concrete action (scan / pick-and-build / add-checks) and the third leg carries new concrete content, not a restatement, so it does not trip the epistrophe-triple ban even under the visible-body test). No 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction. No self-grading superlative (closest is 'grows your kit', a plain functional description, not value-graded). No number-plus-retraction (no numbers in body scope; 'Time: 3 minutes' sits in the maintainer block, out of scope). No abstraction-noun stack ('shapes', 'session', 'prompt', 'kit', 'skill', 'checks' are all concrete). No verb triplet with an empty leg. Nothing to flag on any sub-item.
